name: create_flask_reviews_blueprint
description: Adds a reviews blueprint wired through a new repository and app registration
prompts: This Flask app (package `app`, with create_app() in app/__init__.py, a books blueprint in app/routes/books.py, and BookRepository in app/repository.py) needs a NEW reviews resource across the layers: (1) add a ReviewRepository class to app/repository.py with add(book_id, text) -> dict and list_for_book(book_id) -> list; each review is {"id", "bookId", "text"}, ids auto-increment from 1, list_for_book preserves insertion order and returns [] when none; (2) create app/routes/reviews.py with a Blueprint named reviews_bp exposing POST /reviews (JSON body {bookId, text} -> 201 with the created review) and GET /reviews?bookId=N (200 with the reviews for that book); (3) register reviews_bp in create_app(). Keep POST /books working.

setup_files.app/__init__.py:
from flask import Flask

from app.routes.books import books_bp


def create_app():
    app = Flask(__name__)
    app.register_blueprint(books_bp)
    return app

test_setup_files.test_reviews.py:
from app import create_app

client = create_app().test_client()

r = client.post("/reviews", json={"bookId": 7, "text": "great"})
assert r.status_code == 201, f"POST /reviews: {r.status_code} {r.data}"
assert r.get_json() == {"id": 1, "bookId": 7, "text": "great"}, r.get_json()

assert client.post("/reviews", json={"bookId": 7, "text": "ok"}).get_json()["id"] == 2
client.post("/reviews", json={"bookId": 99, "text": "other"})

r = client.get("/reviews?bookId=7")
assert r.status_code == 200
assert [x["text"] for x in r.get_json()] == ["great", "ok"], r.get_json()
assert client.get("/reviews?bookId=99").get_json()[0]["text"] == "other"

# books still work
assert client.post("/books", json={"title": "T", "author": "A"}).status_code == 201
print("PASS")

reference_solution.app/__init__.py:
from flask import Flask

from app.routes.books import books_bp
from app.routes.reviews import reviews_bp


def create_app():
    app = Flask(__name__)
    app.register_blueprint(books_bp)
    app.register_blueprint(reviews_bp)
    return app
